name: Ragefire Chasm
summary: Beneath Orgrimmar, troggs and a demonic cult threaten the young Horde. The Searing Blade plots in volcanic caverns below the Cleft of Shadow, with the capital above.

sections.title: Subterranean Peril
sections.body: Ragefire troggs burst from deep beneath Orgrimmar into winding volcanic corridors and lava pits. As orcish builders raise their new home above, the troggs grow more aggressive. Magatha Grimtotem sends Maur Grimtotem to speak for Thunder Bluff, but the troggs slaughter him. They yield only to force.

sections.title: The Searing Blade
sections.body: The Searing Blade, a demonic cult, poses a greater danger than the troggs. Loyal to the Shadow Council, its fanatics plot the young Horde's ruin in caverns beside streams of magma. Jergosh the Invoker, a cunning warlock, leads with Bazzalan, a satyr, and Taragaman the Hungerer, a vicious felguard. Taragaman presides over an altar in the lava lake.

sections.title: The Warchief's Game
sections.body:
Neeru Fireblade appears to train warlocks beside the chasm's entrance in the Cleft of Shadow. In secret, he leads the local Burning Blade. He sends Horde adventurers into the depths as tests of loyalty, hoping to cull weak cultists and kill Thrall's supporters.

Thrall knows of Neeru's deception. The Warchief uses these forays to eliminate dangerous cult leaders such as Jergosh and Bazzalan. He keeps Neeru in place to watch the Shadow Council's broader schemes.

faq.q: Where is the entrance to Ragefire Chasm?
faq.answer: The entrance is inside Orgrimmar, in the underground district called the Cleft of Shadow. It lies near the tent of Neeru Fireblade, the warlock trainer.
Ragefire troggs tunneled upward from underground recesses beneath Durotar. Diplomacy failed to quell their sudden presence beneath the capital, where they pose a severe danger.

faq.q: Who leads the cultists inside the chasm?
faq.answer: Jergosh the Invoker, a warlock, and Bazzalan, a satyr, lead the Searing Blade. Taragaman the Hungerer, a summoned felguard, supports them.

faq.q: What does killing Bazzalan and Jergosh accomplish for the story?
faq.answer: Killing Bazzalan and Jergosh breaks the Searing Blade's active leadership beneath Orgrimmar. Their deaths show the Horde's resilience and let Thrall thwart a demon-worshiping cell beneath his throne.

faq.q: Can Alliance adventurers enter Ragefire Chasm?
faq.answer: Any adventurer can physically enter through the portal. An Alliance adventurer must evade high-level Horde guards and hostile defenders throughout Orgrimmar to reach the Cleft of Shadow.

faq.q: Why doesn't Thrall simply execute Neeru Fireblade?
faq.answer: Thrall tolerates those who practice dark magic in the Cleft of Shadow. He keeps them close and under his watch rather than driving them out of sight.

angles.text: For the Horde, cleansing the chasm beneath Orgrimmar gives young champions a trial of strength and a chance to protect the capital.
As a warlock, you can see the Searing Blade's dark magic firsthand in the rites and demonic tomes used by Jergosh the Invoker and Bazzalan.
As a Tauren, you know Maur Grimtotem's death at the hands of the Ragefire troggs makes hunting the beasts a matter of honor and retribution for Thunder Bluff.
